Data Binding

Data binding connects an element property or callback to an object in your application. This allows controls to display and update data without manually copying every value between the model and UI.

Creating a Backend

A backend can be a normal class with public properties and methods. This example uses INotifyPropertyChanged so the UI can be told when a value changes:

Register the instance before compiling:

Name can be read and written. Status has no public setter, so it is read-only to MXML. Save, Submit and the color/file methods are callbacks that controls can call.

Binding Properties

  • TwoWay: Reads and writes a public writable property. This is the default when the source has a public setter.
  • OneWay: Reads the value without writing back. This is the default for read-only properties and methods. Trying to write through a OneWay binding throws an error.
  • OneTime: Copies the value during compilation without installing a live binding.

The shorter form {App.Name} selects the default mode. Bindings apply to the whole value; they do not evaluate arbitrary C# expressions or interpolate a binding into the middle of a string.

Binding endpoints must be public properties, methods or events. Fields, indexers and private members are not supported.

Callbacks and Events

Callback methods must match the delegate or event signature. For example:

Delegate properties call compatible public methods or the current delegate value. CLR control events can call a backend handler. The reverse also works: a public control method can handle a backend event. Overloaded methods are resolved against the expected delegate signature.

A background event is dispatched to the attached window's UI thread. Do not use async void callbacks as a substitute for awaited application work.

Updating Bound Values

INotifyPropertyChanged and INotifyCollectionChanged allow MelonUI to invalidate controls when their data changes. Nested paths are followed again when an intermediate object is replaced. For App.Profile.Name, notify Profile when replacing that object, and notify Name on its new instance when the name changes.

Background notifications queue UI invalidation, but this does not make your model or ordinary lists thread-safe. Manage changes to shared state deliberately, normally on the UI thread.

Plain/static sources and some nested paths use polling. Subscriptions suspend when a control is detached, resume once when it is attached again, and are released after replacement or disposal.

Binding from C#

CreatePath accepts the source instance, a member path and an optional target type. A Type can be supplied for static members. There are also constructors taking PropertyInfo, MethodInfo or EventInfo.

Generated setters write through an installed binding. RemoveBinding removes and disposes that binding.

Values and Conversion

Conversions use invariant culture, so decimal values use a period. Supported values include primitives, enums, nullable values, Guid, TimeSpan, colors, compatible typed arrays and type converters.

  • {Null}: Supplies null to a compatible reference or nullable property.
  • {}: Escapes a literal opening brace.
  • Arrays: Bind a typed array such as App.Peaks; a comma-separated string does not automatically create it.
  • TypeExtensions: Register a host conversion with page.TypeExtensions[typeof(MyType)] when a custom type needs one.

Errors from direct C# binding getters and setters remain visible to the application rather than silently using an old value.
